statement: Subject name is a required positional argument.
Hemisphere is a required positional argument.
Surface name is an optional positional argument.
When the -l label-file option is used, calculations are limited to the specified label.
No flagged arguments are required.
Using -f requires either the -a or -l option to specify input.
Input segmentation volume provided with --seg.
If an input volume is supplied, it must be the same size and dimension as the segmentation volume.
If a mask volume is supplied, it must be the same size and dimension as the segmentation volume.
The FreeSurfer color table file maps each segmentation index to a segmentation name and color.
Partial volume compensation with --pv is usually only done when computing anatomical statistics and is not used with --annot.
If no voxels meet the masking criteria, mri_segstats exits with an error.
If neither --id nor a color table is specified, all IDs from the segmentation volume are used.
If an input volume is supplied, it must be the same size and dimension as the segmentation volume.
If a mask volume is supplied, it must be the same size and dimension as the segmentation volume.
If no voxels meet the masking criteria, the program exits with an error.
With --meas surfmeasure, input is taken from subject/surf/hemi.surfmeasure.
The --fsgd option specifies the input subject list from an FSGD file.
The registration matrix file is of the type accepted or created by tkregister2.
The --target option selects the common-space subject; --hemi selects lh or rh for source and target surfaces.
When subjects are listed using --s, each has its own --s; this option is for use with --meas.
The --is option is an alternative to --meas and still requires a supplied subject list.
For --paired-diff there must be an even number of inputs.
When using full paths with --fsgd, subjects must be in the same order as the input surface files.
--cache-out-only requires supplying a tmpdir.
ANALYZE and NIFTI formats cannot represent a dimension with more than 32k elements.
None of the paired diff options will affect caching.
Source subject name in $SUBJECTS_DIR or ico; input data must have been sampled onto this subject's surface.
File containing the data on the source surface.
Target subject name in $SUBJECTS_DIR or ico for icosahedron.
If source and target subjects differ, the registration surface is used; sphere.reg is the default.
For trg_type w or paint, use the full path for the target file.
With paint output, specify the output file with a partial path or it will be written into the subject's anatomical directory.
The metric file to resample, typically a native-mesh metric.
A sphere surface in register with the new sphere and having the mesh the metric is currently on.
A sphere surface that is the desired output mesh, typically a standard sphere.
The method argument must be one of ADAP_BARY_AREA or BARYCENTRIC.
If ADAP_BARY_AREA is used, exactly one of -area-surfs or -area-metrics must be specified.
The current sphere must be in register with the new sphere.
The -current-roi option only masks the input; the output may be slightly dilated in comparison.
The anatomical input is a structural intensity image, typically T1.
Brain segmentation template: an anatomical intensity template that is not skull-stripped.
Brain extraction probability mask in the segmentation template space; a binary mask is acceptable.
At least four priors must exist, corresponding to CSF, cortical GM, WM and subcortical GM.
Image dimension must be 2 or 3.
If a registration template is supplied with -t, it must be skull-stripped.
If an extraction registration mask is supplied with -f, it is a binary metric mask in the segmentation template space (-e).
At least four prior images are required; fewer causes the script to exit.
The segmentation template and registration template may be different.
If command -v cannot find a dependency program, the script reports an error.
Specified anatomical images are checked for existence.
The script tests each expected output image for existence and records missing outputs.
The script checks for the affine registration transform from the segmentation step.
If a command exits with nonzero status, the script exits unless debug mode is enabled.
For Templateflow priors, if SGM is not found then SCGM is used instead.
Prior combinations are only allowed for gray matter or white matter; other labels cause an error exit.
If the cortical thickness output is not produced, the script exits with an error.
subject id
hemisphere: rh or lh
canonical surface file, e.g. sphere.reg, describing registration of a subject's vertices to the reference average surface
Classifier array input file.
This automatic procedure employs data from a previously-prepared atlas file.
The surface file to resample, typically a native-mesh anatomical or inflated surface.
A sphere surface in register with <new-sphere> that uses the mesh the input surface is currently on, typically a registered native-mesh sphere.
A sphere surface that has the desired output mesh, typically a standard sphere.
The method name, which must be one of ADAP_BARY_AREA or BARYCENTRIC.
If ADAP_BARY_AREA is used, exactly one of -area-surfs or -area-metrics must be specified.
For cut surfaces (including flatmaps), use -surface-cut-resample instead.
Instead of resampling a spherical surface, the -surface-sphere-project-unproject command is recommended.
ADAP_BARY_AREA is not generally recommended for surface resampling, but is provided for completeness.
FIRST needs a good quality T1-weighted image.
Only T1-weighted images can be used as input to run_first_all.
first_flirt should be used on whole-head (non-betted) images.
If the registration stage fails then the model fitting will not work, though run_first_all continues to run and may produce outputs.
When fitting the cerebellum models, a different transformation matrix than that used for the other structures must be input.
The -cort flag must be specified for first_flirt to perform the registration needed for cerebellum models.
The full path name to the model must be used with -m.
Check the log directory error outputs; no output means no errors.
Check registration quality using slicesdir on the registered images.
Pay particular attention to the sub-cortical structures when assessing registrations.
Check segmentation quality with first_roi_slicesdir, which generates a webpage summary.
If there are problems, different segmentation options such as number of modes or boundary correction method can be tried using the individual tools.
Boundary correction method none is appropriate for models in the 05mm subdirectory.
